_comment: Singapore government payout and voucher schemes. These are the highest precision-per-effort signal in the whole project: there is no innocent reason for an arbitrary registrable to contain 'cdcvoucher'. Unlike brands, there is no legitimate long tail to allowlist — each scheme has essentially one official gov.sg home.
why_this_file_exists: SG payout schemes are phished hard around every disbursement cycle, and the lure is the scheme name rather than any brand.
Scheme tokens are long, compound, and have no dictionary collisions, so they can run at high weight with almost no false positives.
Nobody outside Singapore would think to include these, which is a genuine part of the local-focus value proposition.

scoring.note: seasonal_boost applies when the hit falls inside an active disbursement window. A scheme lookalike appearing three weeks before a payout is more interesting than one appearing at a random time of year.

maintenance.why: Schemes are time-bound. New ones are announced at Budget and around National Day; old ones stop being useful lures once disbursement ends. A stale schemes file quietly stops earning its weight.
maintenance.sources: Budget announcements, official scheme microsites under gov.sg, CSA and ScamShield advisories.
maintenance.warning: Scheme names and their exact spellings must be checked against the official site before being added. A misspelled scheme token in this file is a signal that never fires.

schemes.notes: Community Development Council vouchers. Recurring, widely distributed, heavily phished. Highest-value entry in this file.
Credit top-ups are announced periodically and phished around each announcement.

candidates_pending_verification._comment: Names heard but not confirmed against an official source. Do NOT move these into 'schemes' until the exact official spelling is verified — a wrong token is a dead signal that looks alive.
